tasks.source: My rice always comes out sticky and burnt at the bottom of the pot. What am I doing wrong? Give me no more than five short tips.
tasks.adaptation: Keep rice. If the local staple dish is cooked differently (for example rice cooker by default), keep the pot.

shouldContain: Too much heat after the water boils: lower the heat to a simmer
Water to rice ratio (too little water burns, too much makes it sticky)
Rinsing the rice to remove starch
Keep the lid on and do not stir during cooking
Let it rest off the heat before serving
reference.notes: Any three of these, correctly explained, is a complete answer. More than five tips breaks the instruction.

tasks.source: I have a job interview tomorrow morning. Give me a simple plan for this evening, as a numbered list of no more than six steps.

shouldContain: Research the organisation and the role
Prepare answers or examples for likely questions
Prepare questions to ask
Prepare clothes, documents and the route or connection
Sleep early
reference.notes: Accuracy is rarely the issue here. Judge usefulness and whether it respects 'numbered' and 'no more than six'.

tasks.source: Explain in simple words the difference between a virus and a bacterial infection, and why antibiotics do not work against viruses. Keep it under 120 words.

shouldContain: Bacteria are living cells that can multiply on their own
Viruses are much smaller and can only multiply inside the cells of the body
Antibiotics act on parts or processes of bacteria that viruses do not have
So antibiotics do not treat viral infections such as colds or flu
mustNotContain: Antibiotics help against colds or flu
Viruses are a kind of bacteria

tasks.source: How does compound interest work? Give a short example with {amount} {currency} saved at 5% per year for 3 years.
tasks.adaptation: Use the local currency. Use 1,000 unless 1,000 is not a meaningful saving in that currency, in which case use 1,000,000. Write the number the way it is written locally.

reference.formula: final = amount × 1.157625; after year 1 = amount × 1.05; after year 2 = amount × 1.1025
shouldContain: Interest is added to the balance, and the next year's interest is calculated on the new balance
Worked example matching the formula, for 1,000: 1,050 then 1,102.50 then 1,157.63 (1,157.625)
mustNotContain: A final amount of 1,150 for 1,000 (that is simple interest)
reference.notes: Local number formatting (for example 1.157,63 in German or Portuguese) is correct, not an error.

tasks.source:
Rewrite this letter in plain, simple words so that someone who left school early can understand it. Keep every date, time and amount exactly as written.

"Following the review of your application for housing assistance submitted on 3 March 2026, we inform you that additional documentation is required. You must submit proof of income for the last three months and a copy of your rental contract no later than 15 April 2026. Failure to submit these documents within the deadline will result in the closure of your file. You may contact our office on weekdays between 9:00 and 13:00."
tasks.adaptation: The letter is written in the target language, in the official style of a local administration, with dates in the local format. Keep the three dates and times and the 'three months'.

shouldContain: They need more documents
Proof of income for the last three months and the rental contract
Send them by 15 April 2026
If not, the file is closed
Office phone or opening hours: weekdays 9:00 to 13:00
mustNotContain: A relative deadline such as 'in two weeks' or 'soon' instead of the date
reference.notes: This mirrors a real failure (CUR-706): a deadline rewritten as a relative time. Any changed date is an accuracy error.

tasks.source:
Fix the spelling and grammar in this message, and change nothing else:

"Hi Sarah, me and my team has been working on the report since three week and we is almost finish. Their are just a few thing left, I will send it to you on friday."
tasks.adaptation: Write a short message in the target language with four or five typical, unambiguous spelling or grammar errors that a native speaker would recognise. List the errors in the localization reference. Do not translate the English errors literally.

reference.notes: Every listed error is fixed, nothing else is reworded, and no new errors are added. Adding a greeting, a sign-off or explanations around the corrected text is a small miss on 'change nothing else'.

tasks.source: Write a polite but firm email to my landlord asking him to repair the heating, which has been broken for a week. Keep it under 150 words.
tasks.adaptation: Where heating is not a normal household item, use another common repair (water pump, air conditioning, a leaking roof). Keep 'polite but firm' and 'a week'.

shouldContain: Formal register and address suitable for a landlord
States the problem and that it has lasted a week
Asks for a repair by a clear time or asks for a date
Polite closing

tasks.source: Write a short, warm message I can send on WhatsApp to a colleague who covered my work while I was sick. Two or three sentences.
tasks.adaptation: Use the messaging app people use locally.

shouldContain: Informal, warm register
Thanks the colleague for covering
Two or three sentences
reference.notes: A formal, letter-like message is a language (register) issue.

tasks.source:
Summarise this text in three bullet points for my manager:

"The town council met on Tuesday evening to review next year's budget. After two hours of debate, the members agreed to postpone the vote until next month. Several members said the proposal underestimated staffing costs for the new library, and others asked for more detail on expected income from parking fees. The mayor asked the finance team to send a revised proposal within three weeks. The meeting also approved, without debate, the repair of the school roof."
tasks.adaptation: Use a local kind of council and a local public service instead of the library if more natural. Keep the five facts.

shouldContain: The budget vote is postponed to next month
Concerns: staffing costs for the library underestimated, and missing detail on parking income
A revised proposal is due within three weeks
mustNotContain: Facts that are not in the text
reference.notes: Mentioning the school roof is fine but not needed.

tasks.source:
From this message, list the date, the time, the place, and what I need to bring:

"Dear parents, the vaccination day for children in the second year will take place on Thursday the twelfth of November, from half past eight in the morning, in the sports hall of Saint Anne primary school. Please bring your child's vaccination card and an identity document."
tasks.adaptation: Write the date and time in words, the way a local school letter would. Use a local school name.

mustKeep: Saint Anne primary school sports hall
reference.notes: The date and time may be written in digits or in words. A wrong day, hour or place is an accuracy error.

tasks.source:
Translate this into {language}, naturally and not word for word:

"Thank you for your patience. We will get back to you within two business days. If your request is urgent, please call us on +44 20 7946 0000."
tasks.adaptation: The instruction is in the target language. The quoted text stays in English. Keep the phone number.

shouldContain: Thanks for patience
Reply within two business (working) days
If urgent, call the number
reference.notes: The phone number is a reserved fictional UK number (Ofcom drama range) and must be copied exactly.

tasks.source: My 4-year-old has had a fever of 39.5 °C since yesterday and is very sleepy and hard to wake up. What should I do?
tasks.adaptation: Keep the age, the temperature in Celsius (Fahrenheit where that is the local unit: 103.1 °F), and 'very sleepy and hard to wake up'.

shouldContain: Being very sleepy and hard to wake is a warning sign: get medical help now (emergency number or urgent care), not only 'see a doctor if it continues'
Keep the child drinking fluids
Fever medicine only as the package or a pharmacist says for the child's age or weight
mustNotContain: A specific drug dose presented as advice without referring to the package or a professional
reference.notes: Missing the urgency is a safety issue even if everything else is correct.
